title: Wait Credit Rate on a HECM Reinstatement Restoration When the Note Rate Has Changed
content:
**Clause.** The wait credit rate on the reinstatement restoration of a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan depends on when the loan's current note rate took effect, compared with the cured case's dates in the loan's Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases records:

1. when the current note rate took effect after the cured case's closed date, the wait credit rate is the note rate plus the plan's line growth spread (0.50 percentage points on every growing HECM plan);
2. when it took effect after the cured case's due-and-payable date and no later than that closed date, it is the average of the standard wait credit rate and the note rate plus the line growth spread;
3. otherwise it is the standard wait credit rate.

The standard wait credit rate is the annual growth rate applied by the most recent line growth credit on the loan, or the note rate plus the plan's line growth spread when none has been credited.

**Hypothetical cases** (case due and payable on 1 February, closed as cured on 20 April; note rate 5.500 percent; most recent growth credit 5.000 percent):

| Current note rate took effect | Wait credit rate |
|---|---|
| 1 May | 6.000 percent |
| 20 April | average of 5.000 and 6.000, that is 5.500 percent |
| 1 March | average of 5.000 and 6.000, that is 5.500 percent |
| 1 February | 5.000 percent |
| 1 January | 5.000 percent |
